checks.finding: REQ-005 (requirements.md:174-179) delegates the Pack's capability IDs, predicates, facets, review checks, gates, Lite policy, enforcement minimum, and delivery strategy to the resolved OQ-006 decision. OQ-006 (requirements.md:543-569) names two capability IDs and states broad composition/Lite/delivery rules, but does not specify the predicates, facets, review checks, or gates; its dated clarification says those details remain unchanged without enumerating them, while also noting the current Registry has no developer-tooling or cli-library entries. An implementer and verifier therefore cannot determine the expected Pack contract. This is a Phase 1 specification gap because AC-008 relies on that contract as its oracle; the missing details can produce materially different Pack behavior.

Each stated goal has a corresponding requirement and acceptance criterion: Phase 1 Context (REQ-001/AC-001–002), inventory and ownership (REQ-002–003/AC-003–006, AC-032), characteristics (REQ-004/AC-007, AC-030–031), Pack and advisory dogfood (REQ-005–006/AC-008–011, AC-027), promotion and rollback (REQ-007–009/AC-012–018, AC-028, AC-033–034), friction capture (REQ-010/AC-019, AC-029), and dependency/platform/provenance conditions (REQ-011–014/AC-020–026).

AC-008 (requirements.md:302) accepts a “human-approved first Pack” and resolves it for a representative change, but does not give that Pack's expected predicate, facet, review-check, or gate behavior. OQ-006 (requirements.md:543-569) also does not enumerate those values, and the dated clarification states the current Registry lacks the two capabilities. A test can observe that some Pack resolves, but cannot decide whether it resolves correctly. This is a specification-review issue because the acceptance oracle is incomplete before implementation; the omitted contract can cause downstream implementations and verification to disagree.

Requirements explicitly exclude creating a live Context during bootstrap, later Packs, replacing core Registry/ownership/Manifest/approval machinery, adding UI/cloud/new CI, and approving specs, tasks, sidecars, or WFIs (requirements.md:274-280). AC-009 also bounds the Pack exclusions.

The requirements state approval and protected-copy boundaries, dependency and mutable shared-state re-verification, cross-platform/Bash/PowerShell coverage, data-classification omissions, rollback identity/cooldown/signature rules, and the prohibition on agent approval of protected records and WFIs. These give downstream work concrete constraints.

High-risk approval, rollback, ownership, promotion, stale-evidence, and enforcement claims have planned validation surfaces: AC-002, AC-005–006, AC-013, AC-015–018, AC-020–021, AC-032–034, and the platform/regression criteria AC-022–024. Tests are marked Planned, appropriately distinguishing specification from execution evidence.
